title: MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.028 (the sqrt-batch rescale that was never applied)
description: One constant: Muon MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.028 (-30%) at the true baseline (HEAD_DIM 128, WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5, DEPTH 10, 2^18, device batch 64). Nothing else. val_bpb 0.988612 vs 0.988076 baseline: a tie, +0.0005.
reflection:
All six agents proposed the identical WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.7, so I dropped my own copy of it and defected to the same hypothesis on a different knob, measured independently against the shared 0.988076 baseline.

Result: MATRIX_LR -30% is a DEAD TIE. val_bpb 0.988612 (+0.000536), final smoothed train loss 2.7538 vs the baseline's 2.752, and identical 1119 steps / 293.3M tokens / 41.98% MFU / 34.6GB. The matched step count makes this the cleanest paired comparison in the cell: nothing moved.

What that means, and it is not what my proposal predicted. The Muon LR curve is ASYMMETRIC and we now have three points around 0.04: +50% costs +0.0032, +37% costs +0.0056, -30% costs +0.0005. Sharp on the high side, flat on the low side - the textbook shape of an LR optimum sitting at or just below the current value. So MATRIX_LR is already right and the axis is CLOSED; nobody should spend another slot on it, in either direction. It also kills the specific story I argued from: the batch halving in round 0 did NOT leave the Muon LR mistuned, because rescaling it by sqrt(0.5) buys exactly nothing.

The useful by-product is a decomposition for the six warmdown-0.7 arms. 'Effective LR is too high' predicts that cutting the LR integral helps. I cut the Muon integral by 30% and got nothing. So if warmdown 0.7 wins, the gain is the ANNEAL SHAPE (more of the budget spent approaching zero), not the LR magnitude - and the follow-up is WARMDOWN 1.0, not a global LR cut. If warmdown 0.7 loses, both knobs are at their optimum and the entire optimization block should be treated as tuned, leaving only regions nobody has touched.

I also retracted my own outstanding max-autotune claim (#104) rather than spend a slot on it: inductor only re-tunes GEMMs (attention is FA3, Muon's NS iterations are a separate compiled region), realistic upside is 0-5% tokens, token sensitivity near the baseline is ~5e-4 per few percent, and autotuning risks the 900s wall clock. Bad use of 1 of 19 slots. If anyone wants throughput, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 -> 128 (grad_accum 2 -> 1) is the free version with no compile gamble.
